A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TRACE-RPS research paper, with complete main text and Appendices A–J. All 24 pages were compared; text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of TRACE, RPS, and MPS, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, robustness experiments, and the authors' Reddit-data evaluation in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including the real-world evaluation, robustness tests, and case studies.

M1.justification: TRACE's vocabulary extraction and inference-chain anonymization, the RPS and MPS optimization procedures, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The wording edit in Section 4.1 does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Synthetic, SynthPAI, and the authors' real-world Reddit data. Attribute coverage and the prompt-variation, transfer, positional, and adaptive-attack scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain No Defense, Azure, Dou-SD, D-Defense, and FgAA. Appendix E retains both adaptive attacks; renaming SuffixDrop-k to SuffixDrop-ℓ does not change its procedure or comparator membership.

E3.justification: Tables 8–9 revise the reported evaluation-model label from Llama3-8B-Instruct to Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, aligning it with Section 5.1 in both versions. This is a limited correction to reported model identification, not evidence of rerunning experiments; other evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component and Top-K ablations, robustness and transfer analyses, iteration discussion, and Appendix J case studies are retained. SuffixDrop still uses the same truncation lengths despite its notation correction.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical values, plotted results, and qualitative case-study outputs are retained. For example, Table 9 keeps SuffixDrop accuracies of 27.43% and 0.76% and LLMSanitize accuracies of 23.62% and 33.90%; only labels are corrected.

T1.justification: The formal objectives, definitions, and Equations (1)–(15) are unchanged. Appendix B removes the repeated explanation that I[·] denotes the indicator function, which remains defined after Equation (3); no mathematical content is lost.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about privacy protection, model transferability, prompt robustness, and utility–privacy tradeoffs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of anonymization limits, refusal-based protection, instruction-following models, adaptive attacks, and utility tradeoffs are unchanged. No applicability boundary or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: The implementation guidance, optimization budgets and thresholds, hardware, decoding settings, stopping criteria, prompts, and code-access information are retained. The model named in the corrected appendix headings was already disclosed in Section 5.1.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning of TRACE-RPS relative to anonymization and prompt-optimization research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited copyedits: 'Given an input user text' becomes 'Given a user text,' redundant indicator-function prose is removed, SuffixDrop notation is harmonized, and Table 10's caption gains 'the.' Section organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 7's Closed-Source heading is recentered, Tables 8–9 receive corrected labels and slight width adjustments, and Table 10's caption is lightly edited. Local text reflow occurs, while all figures and the overall document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reporting clarity by resolving the appendix model-label inconsistency with Section 5.1, matching SuffixDrop's name to its defined parameter, and correcting Table 7's heading alignment. These limited corrections improve internal consistency without changing the scientific evidence or claims.
